explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. Jesus says, “You believe in God; believe in Me as well.” (John 14:1) Notice He doesn't ask them to trade one for the other. He says “as well,” so it's both, side by side.

explanations.answer: Wait for Him in the city
explanations.explanation: Not this time, friend. Nothing in these verses sends the disciples to wait in a city. Jesus tells them, “Do not let your hearts be troubled,” and then asks them to believe in Him as well. The ask is about their trust, not their location.

Close to the mood of the night, but that's not what He says here. Jesus tells the disciples to believe in Him as well as in God (John 14:1). I think a troubled heart needs somewhere to rest, and He gives them that first. No night shift is assigned.

That's it, baker. Jesus says, “I am going there to prepare a place for you?” (John 14:2) He's talking about a spot made ready for the disciples, in His Father's house. One little word, and it holds a lot of comfort.

I see why you'd go there, because Jesus does talk about a way in a minute. But in verse 2 He says He is going to prepare a place for them. The road talk comes up when Thomas asks his question. Same conversation, different word.

Good guess for a house talk, but the word isn't there. Jesus says, “In My Father’s house are many rooms.” (John 14:2) He goes on to say He is going there to prepare a place for them. Rooms and a place, no temple in sight.

Right, baker. Jesus says, “I will come back and welcome you into My presence, so that you also may be where I am.” (John 14:3) He goes ahead, and then He comes back. The point is that they end up where He is.

It's actually true, friend. Jesus says, “I will come back and welcome you into My presence, so that you also may be where I am.” (John 14:3) He doesn't leave them waiting without a promise. He says He's coming back for them.

explanations.answer: We don't even know where You're going
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Thomas says, “we do not know where You are going, so how can we know the way?” (John 14:5) He says out loud what I bet a few others were thinking. I think a lot of us would have kept nodding.

explanations.answer: We'll follow You wherever You go
explanations.explanation: That sounds brave, but Thomas doesn't say it. He says, “we do not know where You are going, so how can we know the way?” (John 14:5) He's asking a question, not making a promise. He says plainly that he doesn't know.

explanations.answer: Then take us there with You now
explanations.explanation: Nice try, friend. Thomas doesn't ask to go along right then. He says, “we do not know where You are going, so how can we know the way?” (John 14:5) His question is about knowing the way.

explanations.answer: The way and the truth and the life
explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. Jesus answers, “I am the way and the truth and the life.” (John 14:6) Thomas asked about a way, and Jesus points to Himself. It's not directions to a place, it's a Person.

explanations.answer: The guide and the lamp and the key
explanations.explanation: Those are handy things to have, friend, but they aren't His words. Jesus says, “I am the way and the truth and the life.” (John 14:6) Three things, yes, just different ones. I'd have bet on the lamp too.

explanations.answer: The guard and the scroll and the seal
explanations.explanation: That list has a nice official ring to it, but it isn't what Jesus says. His answer to Thomas is, “I am the way and the truth and the life.” (John 14:6) No guard, no scroll, no seal. Just Him.
Not quite, baker. Jesus says, “No one comes to the Father except through Me.” (John 14:6) He doesn't give a list of ways. He says He is the way.

That's right. Right after saying He is the way and the truth and the life, Jesus says, “No one comes to the Father except through Me.” (John 14:6) He doesn't offer Thomas a menu of ways. He gives one, and it's Himself.
Yes, baker. Philip says, “Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.” (John 14:8) He asks for one thing and says it would be enough. Jesus has more to say about that.
Philip isn't thinking that big here. He says, “Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.” (John 14:8) It's about “us,” the disciples at the table. Nothing about a sign for the world.

Close, friend, but Philip doesn't mention the others. He says, “Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.” (John 14:8) The word he uses is “us.” He's asking for himself and the men sitting around him.

explanations.answer: How can you say show us the Father
explanations.explanation: That's it, baker. Jesus asks, “How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?” (John 14:9) He's just said that anyone who has seen Him has seen the Father. So the question is a gentle nudge to look at who is standing right there.

explanations.answer: Why do you ask Me for a sign
explanations.explanation: Not what He says, friend. Philip never asked for a sign, and Jesus never mentions one here. He asks, “How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?” (John 14:9) He's answering Philip's exact words.

explanations.answer: Where do you think I am going
explanations.explanation: That's closer to Thomas's moment than Philip's. Jesus asks Philip, “How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?” (John 14:9) The question is about seeing the Father, not about where Jesus is headed. I'd say this one stays right on Philip's own request.

It's the other way around, baker. Jesus says, “The words I say to you, I do not speak on My own.” (John 14:10) He says it is the Father dwelling in Him, performing His works. So the words aren't just coming from Him alone.

Yes, that's right. Jesus says, “The words I say to you, I do not speak on My own. Instead, it is the Father dwelling in Me, performing His works.” (John 14:10) The Father is at work in Him. Whatever He says, it isn't a solo act.

You've got it, baker. Jesus says, “…or at least believe on account of the works themselves.” (John 14:11) He gives them another reason to believe. If His word isn't enough yet, the works are right there to look at.
Actually it's true, friend. Jesus says, “…or at least believe on account of the works themselves.” (John 14:11) He points them to the works as a reason to believe. It's right there in His words.

Right, baker. Jesus says, “And I will do whatever you ask in My name, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.” (John 14:13) The asking is in His name. And the purpose He gives is that the Father may be glorified in the Son.

I see where that came from. Jesus does use “presence” a few lines earlier, when He says He'll welcome them into His presence (John 14:3). But here He says He will do whatever they ask in His name (John 14:13). Same night, different word.
That word is in the neighborhood, friend. “My Father’s house” was in verse 2. Here it's, “And I will do whatever you ask in My name.” (John 14:13) Keep the house, it just belongs to another verse.

Yes, baker. Jesus says the Father will give them “another Advocate” to be with them forever (John 14:16). A few verses later He names Him as the Holy Spirit (John 14:26). So they won't be on their own.

Interesting guess, friend, but that isn't what Jesus says. He says the Father will give them “another Advocate” to be with them forever (John 14:16). Verse 26 names that Advocate as the Holy Spirit. A prophet isn't mentioned.

I get the thought, but no angel shows up in this passage. Jesus says the Father will give them “another Advocate” to be with them forever (John 14:16). He calls Him the Spirit of truth in the next verse. So the answer is the Advocate.

It's the opposite, baker. Jesus says, “But you do know Him, for He abides with you and will be in you.” (John 14:17) The world can't receive Him, but the disciples do know Him. That's a real difference.
That's right. Jesus says of the Spirit, “But you do know Him, for He abides with you and will be in you.” (John 14:17) The world neither sees Him nor knows Him. The disciples know Him.
Yes, baker. Jesus says, “In a little while the world will see Me no more, but you will see Me.” (John 14:19) The world and the disciples get different news there. Listen for that “but.”

Not this time, friend. Jesus says, “In a little while the world will see Me no more, but you will see Me.” (John 14:19) The world stops seeing Him, and the disciples will see Him. That “but” is doing a lot of work.

That's right, baker. Jesus says, “The one who loves Me will be loved by My Father, and I will love him and reveal Myself to him.” (John 14:21) The Father loves that person, and Jesus loves him too. That's quite a table to be sitting at.

Actually it's true, friend. Jesus says, “The one who loves Me will be loved by My Father, and I will love him and reveal Myself to him.” (John 14:21) The Father's love is right there in His words. Jesus adds His own love and says He will reveal Himself.

explanations.answer: Why reveal Yourself to us and not the world
explanations.explanation: Right, baker. Judas, the disciple who is not Iscariot, asks, “Lord, why are You going to reveal Yourself to us and not to the world?” (John 14:22) It's a fair question, and Jesus answers it right away.

explanations.answer: When will You reveal Yourself to us
explanations.explanation: Good question, but it isn't the one Judas asks. Judas, the disciple who is not Iscariot, says, “Lord, why are You going to reveal Yourself to us and not to the world?” (John 14:22) His question is about why, and about the world being left out. Not about timing.

explanations.answer: How will we know that it is You
explanations.explanation: That's a thoughtful guess, friend. But Judas, the disciple who is not Iscariot, asks, “Lord, why are You going to reveal Yourself to us and not to the world?” (John 14:22) He's asking why, not how. The world is part of his question.
Yes, baker. Jesus says, “If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word.” (John 14:23) That's the first blank. A person who loves Him keeps what He says.

That's the one. Jesus says the Father and He “will come to him and make Our home with him.” (John 14:23) The Father and Jesus making a home with the one who loves Him. I think that's the best part of the verse.

The Sabbath is a real and important word in the Bible, friend, but it doesn't show up in this verse. Jesus says whoever loves Him will keep His word, and that They will make Their home with him (John 14:23). The Sabbath isn't part of this answer.

That's a big Bible word, baker, but it isn't in this verse. Jesus says, “If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word.” (John 14:23) Then He says the Father and He will make Their home with that person. No covenant here.

A throne sounds grand, friend, but that's not what Jesus talks about here. He says the Father and He will “come to him and make Our home with him.” (John 14:23) It's about a home. The word that goes in the first blank is “word.”

explanations.answer: It comes from the One who sent Him
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. Jesus says, “The word that you hear is not My own, but it is from the Father who sent Me.” (John 14:24) The Father is the source of what the disciples are hearing.

explanations.answer: It is meant only for the twelve
explanations.explanation: Jesus doesn't say that, friend. He says, “The word that you hear is not My own, but it is from the Father who sent Me.” (John 14:24) He tells them where it comes from. He doesn't say who is allowed to hear it.

explanations.answer: It will be sealed for a later day
explanations.explanation: Nothing in these verses says that. Jesus says, “The word that you hear is not My own, but it is from the Father who sent Me.” (John 14:24) He's talking about where it comes from. Nothing gets locked away.

Yes, baker. Jesus says the Advocate “will teach you all things and will remind you of everything I have told you.” (John 14:26) Teaching and reminding, both coming from the Spirit. Good news for anybody who's walked into a room and forgotten why.

It's true, friend. Jesus says the Advocate “will teach you all things and will remind you of everything I have told you.” (John 14:26) The reminding part is right there in His words. The Holy Spirit does both.

explanations.answer: He does not give as the world gives
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. Jesus says, “I do not give to you as the world gives.” (John 14:27) He says it right after “Peace I leave with you; My peace I give to you.” His peace is His own.

explanations.answer: He gives only to those who ask
explanations.explanation: That's not in the verse, friend. Jesus says, “Peace I leave with you; My peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives.” (John 14:27) He says He gives His peace, and He puts no asking condition on it. What He does say is that it isn't the world's way of giving.

explanations.answer: He gives it for a little while
explanations.explanation: He doesn't say that here, baker. Jesus says, “Peace I leave with you; My peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives.” (John 14:27) No time limit is attached. The contrast is with the world.
Yes, baker. Jesus says, “If you loved Me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father…” (John 14:28) He tells them to rejoice about where He's going. He says the Father is greater than He is.

I get why, since He's just said not to let their hearts be troubled. But He says, “If you loved Me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father…” (John 14:28) He doesn't call for worry. Verse 27 even says, “do not be afraid.”

That fits the mood of the night, friend. But Jesus says, “If you loved Me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father…” (John 14:28) The word is “rejoice.” It's an invitation to see where He's going and be glad.

explanations.answer: So the world may know He loves the Father
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. Jesus says, “But I do exactly what the Father has commanded Me, so that the world may know that I love the Father.” (John 14:31) He gives the reason Himself. Obeying the Father shows His love for the Father.

explanations.answer: So the disciples will stay beside Him
explanations.explanation: Jesus doesn't give that reason, friend. He says, “But I do exactly what the Father has commanded Me, so that the world may know that I love the Father.” (John 14:31) The reason He gives is about the world knowing His love for the Father. Nothing about keeping anyone close.

explanations.answer: So the prince of this world will flee
explanations.explanation: The prince of this world is mentioned in verse 30, so I see why that came to mind. Jesus says the prince of this world is coming and has no claim on Him. But the reason He gives is, “so that the world may know that I love the Father.” (John 14:31)
